idiom_name: struct + validating constructor function + hand-written `_equal`/`_hash` functions
implementation_notes: C has no operator overloading and does not even define `==` for structs, so equality is written field by field as ordinary functions (`money_equal`, `money_hash`) beside the type, and a validating constructor function replaces the class constructor. The compiler does provide the value half of the pattern natively - struct assignment copies the whole value, and a struct can be returned by value - so the classic 'immutable class with equals/hashCode' collapses into a struct plus free functions; the classic form is still justified when the layout must be hidden behind an opaque handle (ABI stability), in which case only the functions remain public.
pitfalls: Never compare structs with memcmp: padding bytes hold indeterminate values and IEEE-754 -0.0/NaN break byte equality, so equality must be field by field (SEI CERT EXP42-C).
Struct assignment copies every member; for large values pass a const pointer instead of by value, and state the ownership rule in the header so callers do not alias the same buffer.
Without a constructor function the invariant is unenforceable - nothing stops callers from assigning fields directly, so keep the struct definition and fields private to the module.
